title: Substitution of admissible words in structural coefficient squares
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$, a coefficient datum $C$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_{C.\ell}$, and the independently fixed operation models $o$ [def-sf-generator-reduction-data]. Fix universe levels $s,i$. For every finite-type $D.k$-scheme family $W:S\to\mathrm{Scheme}$ with $S:\mathrm{Type}_s$, input locations $\lambda:I\to S$ with $I:\mathrm{Type}_i$, let $B_{\mathrm{int}}$, $B(\mathcal R K)$, $r_B$ and the canonical integral and system generator maps be the word evaluations and comparisons of [def-sf-generator-reduction-data]. Use the predicate Structural and its family StructuralSquares of [lem-sf-open-interchange-reduction-squares]: exactly tensor associativity, two scalar unitors, pullback and proper direct-image composition, and the units and counits of proper pullback/direct image and of quasi-compact open extension/restriction. Assume the coefficient square Assertion for each of these generators whenever both endpoint words have length at most three, for every such family and input family satisfying Admissible and both endpoint Word.admissible with common cohomological and Tor intervals. Then the same structural coefficient squares hold for every finite pair of endpoint words, with the same input and endpoint admissibility hypotheses, without a length bound. No open base-change, open-tensor, proper/open interchange or proper/open restriction square is asserted. No preservation of admissibility for unrelated words is assumed.

proof.text: Induct through the substituted child words. Normalize each actual whole system and use the actual reduction/total-limit reconstruction equivalence. Tensor and pullback use the defining quotient-tower identifications; proper image is the actual total limit. The normalized DVR effectivity and the compatible etale origins, constructible reductions and common finite intervals reconstruct a complete constructible finite-Tor integral vertex. The open reconstruction and reduction comparison supply the same assertion for open extension, including the scalar unit. Each reconstructed finite reduction is the original system level, so support and Tor bounds stay unchanged. This is the same finite induction as the short-intermediate domain argument, without using its length restriction.

Identify the canonical coefficient map of each child with its recursive r. For tensor and pullback transpose the quotient augmentation identity using the actual adjunction; for proper image use its actual counit; for open extension transpose u followed by L(r_j), and use the inverse open reconstruction laws. The counit of a normalized system is invertible. The completion units on complete finite-Tor constructible objects are invertible. Induction and preservation of isomorphisms by each functor and both tensor slots therefore give invertibility of both the recursive completion transport and r at every substituted child. The equations are natural on whole systems, before finite evaluation.

Replace the one or three child words of a structural generator by independent variables at their schemes, retaining the scalar unit in a unitor. Use a finite family lifted to the input universe i. The resulting skeletons have at most two operations. Give these variables the reconstructed actual integral child values. Transport the original intermediate systems by the preceding r isomorphisms. Normalization, origins, support and Tor amplitude are invariant under isomorphism, so these inputs and skeleton endpoints satisfy exactly the assumed short-square domain. Apply the hypothesized short-square family.

Paste the short square with the naturality squares of the system and ringed structural generators and the recursive completion transports. At a unary constructor its coefficient comparison is r_A followed by A(r_child); at tensor it is r_tensor followed by tensor(r_left,r_right). Thus the pasted vertical arrows are exactly r_B and r_C. The ringed naturality and completion transport cancel the child completion isomorphisms in the definition of integralMap. Functoriality and associativity give Assertion for the substituted words. Naturality of tensor constraints follows from their actual ringed constructions; naturality of compositors and adjunction units/counits follows from the specified Hom bijections. Repeated variables use diagonal substitution. Identity maps, empty opens, zero inputs and empty initial input families are covered by the same equations.

lean.statement:
theorem structuralReductionWordSubstitution
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} (coeff : D.CoefficientDatum)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic coeff.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic coeff.l) E] (o : GeneratorReduction.Operations coeff.l E)
    (hShort : ∀ {S : Type s} (W : S → Scheme.{u})
      (_hW : GeneratorReduction.FiniteTypeFamily W D.k)
      {I : Type i} (location : I → S)
      {a : S} {B C : GeneratorReduction.Word W location a}
      (g : GeneratorReduction.GeneratorKind W location B C),
      Structural g → B.length ≤ 3 → C.length ≤ 3 →
      ∀ (K : ∀ k : I, DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource coeff.l E (W (location k))))
        (lo hi torLo torHi : ℤ),
        (∀ k : I, GeneratorReduction.Admissible coeff.l E
          (IntegralSystemRealization.calculus coeff.l E (W (location k))) (K k)
          lo hi torLo torHi) →
        B.admissible coeff.l E W location o K lo hi torLo torHi →
        C.admissible coeff.l E W location o K lo hi torLo torHi →
        GeneratorReduction.Assertion coeff.l E W location o K g) :
    StructuralSquares.{u, s, i} coeff.l E D o
